For Mitti Labs, the deal secures a buyer for 500,000 credits and support to expand its digital twin datasets. For Salesforce, it adds rated, satellite-verified methane credits to its effort to direct capital toward high-impact mitigation. If deliveries meet that verification standard, the contract could become a reference deal for winning buyers toward Mitti Labs’ 2028 issuance goal.

articles.title: Deutsche Bank Books €1.9 Billion Q3 Profit as Sustainable Finance Hits €32 Billion
articles.summary:
Deutsche Bank posted €1.9 billion in third-quarter 2026 profit after tax, its third straight record quarter. Profit before tax rose 8% year on year to €2.6 billion, on net revenues […]
The post Deutsche Bank Books €1.9 Billion Q3 Profit as Sustainable Finance Hits €32 Billion appeared first on ESG News.
articles.full_text:
Deutsche Bank Books €1.9 Billion Q3 Profit as Sustainable Finance Hits €32 Billion
- Record quarterly profit: Profit after tax reached €1.9 billion in the third quarter of 2026, the bank’s third consecutive record quarter.
- Sustainable finance high: Sustainable and transition finance volumes excluding DWS hit €32 billion, the highest for any quarter.
- Capital position: The CET1 ratio stood at 14.0%, at the high end of the bank’s operating range.
Deutsche Bank posted €1.9 billion in third-quarter 2026 profit after tax, its third straight record quarter. Profit before tax rose 8% year on year to €2.6 billion, on net revenues up 4% at €8.3 billion. Meanwhile, sustainable and transition finance volumes excluding DWS hit €32 billion, a quarterly high since the strategy’s launch.
For the first nine months, after-tax profit reached a record €5.9 billion, up 7%, with all four businesses growing profit. Assets under management (AuM) rose €50 billion in the quarter to €2.0 trillion on record net inflows of €47 billion. Post-tax return on tangible equity (RoTE), a core profitability measure, was 10.6%, versus 10.7% a year earlier. “We are pleased to report our third consecutive record quarterly profit in 2026. We grew revenues with outperformance in our focused growth areas, captured record inflows in our asset-gathering businesses, and achieved strong volume growth in loans and deposits. We see encouraging momentum in Germany, where increasing confidence among clients is creating further growth opportunities for us. As a result, nine-month 2026 RoTE improved to 11.5% with all four businesses delivering RoTE above 12%. This performance positions us to meet our 2026 objectives, and further reinforces our confidence that we have upside to our RoTE target of above 13% in 2028,” said Christian Sewing, Chief Executive Officer of Deutsche Bank.
Quick anonymous worklife pollWhat's my daily work emissions burn, or savings?Powered by ESG News
The Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) ratio, a key capital strength measure, stood at 14.0%, at the high end of its operating range. Credit loss provisions rose 9% quarter on quarter to €501 million, reflecting commercial real estate de-risking and an idiosyncratic Corporate Bank event. Noninterest expenses were flat at €5.2 billion, as €0.2 billion of efficiencies largely offset €0.3 billion of new investment. “We have delivered a solid performance across all four businesses, positioning us to achieve our 2026 objectives, and attracted record inflows of € 103 billion in our asset gathering businesses. We are demonstrating strict capital discipline through proactive portfolio measures and rigorous implementation of SVA. We are returning capital to shareholders as planned, and our cost discipline is evident as we continue to self-fund investments through cost efficiencies and build our scalable operating model,” said Raja Akram, Chief Financial Officer of Deutsche Bank.
What’s New in Sustainable Finance
For the first time, the total included €7 billion of private client investments in companies with particularly stringent sustainability criteria. Transition finance, added to the bank’s framework in 2026, contributed €6.4 billion, up from €4.3 billion in the second quarter. As a result, cumulative volumes since January 1, 2020 rose to €555 billion, from €523 billion in Q2. Deals included a €2.6 billion European Green Bond for TenneT Germany, a €1 billion ENERCON guarantee facility and a €375 million loan to Benin.
RELATED ARTICLE: Deutsche Bank Backs $60M Queensland Battery Project
Why It Matters
Deutsche Bank said nine-month revenues of €25.5 billion support its full-year ambition of above €33 billion. Also, Private Bank client assets reached €865 billion, against a 2028 target of €1 trillion. Because private client sustainable equities now count, further Private Bank inflows could lift sustainable finance totals, if clients keep choosing those products.

articles.title: Microsoft Signs On as Sole Buyer for Two Blueleaf Solar Projects in Japan
articles.summary:
Blueleaf Energy, a portfolio company of Macquarie Asset Management (Macquarie), has signed two solar power deals with Microsoft in Japan. Microsoft will be the sole offtaker, or only buyer of […]
The post Microsoft Signs On as Sole Buyer for Two Blueleaf Solar Projects in Japan appeared first on ESG News.
articles.full_text:
Microsoft Signs On as Sole Buyer for Two Blueleaf Solar Projects in Japan
- Japan solar deals: Microsoft will take all the power from two Blueleaf Energy solar projects in Japan under long-term power purchase agreements.
- Macquarie coordination: Macquarie’s Energy Markets and Customer Solutions team structured the agreements for its portfolio company.
- Existing Microsoft portfolio: Projects supporting Microsoft in the UK, Spain and India total 540 MW of wind and solar capacity.
Blueleaf Energy, a portfolio company of Macquarie Asset Management (Macquarie), has signed two solar power deals with Microsoft in Japan. Microsoft will be the sole offtaker, or only buyer of the output, under long-term power purchase agreements (PPAs). Blueleaf is developing both projects, while Macquarie’s Energy Markets and Customer Solutions team coordinated the deals. The companies did not disclose the projects’ capacity, locations, contract length, pricing or expected start of operations.
The agreements build on a relationship focused on powering Microsoft’s expanding business with new clean, cost-efficient generation. Since 2020, the two have worked together to secure offtake deals from projects built by Macquarie’s portfolio companies. “These agreements reflect a relationship that has grown through successful collaboration across multiple markets. We are pleased to work with Microsoft again, supporting its business goals through tailored clean energy solutions that help meet growing global demand for cost-efficient, low-carbon power that can be delivered quickly,” said Ed Northam, Global Head of MAM Green Investments at Macquarie.
Quick anonymous worklife pollWhat's my daily work emissions burn, or savings?Powered by ESG News
“Our collaboration with Microsoft is more than a commercial agreement; it is a shared blueprint for a decarbonised future. By bridging the energy landscapes of Japan and India, we are setting a new benchmark for how regional expertise and collaboration can accelerate the delivery of much-needed new generation capacity. These new PPAs in Japan stem from a trust built on the foundation of our successful delivery of the Pachora Hybrid Power Project in India,” said Raghuram Natarajan, CEO of Blueleaf Energy.
Macquarie linked the deals to rising electricity demand from computing power, AI and digital infrastructure. It cited International Energy Agency (IEA) projections that AI-driven demand will reach 950 TWh (terawatt-hours) by 2030. That is up from 485 TWh in 2025 and would equal 3 per cent of global electricity demand. The IEA also forecasts that renewables will meet nearly 50 per cent of this extra demand, given their cost and timeline advantages.
RELATED ARTICLE: Microsoft Signs Long-Term Washington Solar PPA
Macquarie’s Microsoft Track Record
The Energy Markets and Customer Solutions team structures tailored PPAs that let Macquarie portfolio companies supply global corporates. Active across Europe, the Americas, Asia and Australia, it has delivered more than 8 GW of renewable energy in 15 markets. That includes four renewable energy collaborations with Microsoft since 2020. Before Japan, projects supporting Microsoft spanned the UK, Spain and India, with a combined 540 MW of wind and solar capacity.
Why It Matters
For Blueleaf, the agreements lock in a single long-term buyer for two Japanese solar projects still in development. For Macquarie, they add Japan to the markets where its portfolio companies supply power to Microsoft. If both projects reach operation, Blueleaf could cite them, as it did Pachora, to place more of its pipeline with Microsoft.

articles.title: PureTerra II Secures €30 Million EIF Commitment to Scale Europe’s Water Tech
articles.summary:
The European Investment Fund (EIF) has committed €30 million to PureTerra II, an early-stage venture capital fund for water technologies. The Netherlands-based fund invests primarily in Europe and succeeds a […]
The post PureTerra II Secures €30 Million EIF Commitment to Scale Europe’s Water Tech appeared first on ESG News.
articles.full_text:
PureTerra II Secures €30 Million EIF Commitment to Scale Europe’s Water Tech
- EIF commitment: The European Investment Fund has committed €30 million to PureTerra II, a Netherlands-based water technology fund.
- Pilot-to-scale focus: The fund backs early-stage ventures ready to move from pilot to full-scale industrial deployment.
- InvestEU support: The European Commission’s InvestEU programme supports the EIF commitment.
The European Investment Fund (EIF) has committed €30 million to PureTerra II, an early-stage venture capital fund for water technologies. The Netherlands-based fund invests primarily in Europe and succeeds a fund the EIF also backed in 2021. The commitment, supported by the Commission’s InvestEU programme, was signed at European Water Technology Week in Leeuwarden. The EIF did not disclose PureTerra II’s target size, its other investors or a final close timeline.
PureTerra II’s managers are among the first European venture capital teams dedicated exclusively to water. Job van Schelven, Partner at PureTerra, said: “Europe already has the technology. Four in every ten water patents worldwide come from here, and far too few of them ever reach industrial scale.” He added: “The constraint is capital and adoption, not ideas. With the EIF behind us we can take proven European water technology from pilot to full-scale deployment, which is where it starts to matter for Europe’s water security and for the industry that depends on it.”
Quick anonymous worklife pollWhat's my daily work emissions burn, or savings?Powered by ESG News
The EIF ties the fund to pressure on clean water after one of the warmest and driest summers on record. Water scarcity and pollution are already raising costs for factories, farms and water utilities. “A fund like this one could hardly be more topical at this point in time,” said Marjut Falkstedt, Chief Executive of the EIF. “Europe’s water resources are under enormous pressure, closely related not only to climate change but also our excessive use of this scarce and crucial element.”
The European Commission estimates that meeting existing EU water rules requires an additional €23 billion of investment every year. Public funds cannot fill that gap alone, according to the EIF. Regulation also sets a deadline: the recast Urban Wastewater Treatment Directive obliges utilities and industry to adopt advanced treatment within a fixed period. So does the PFAS restriction under REACH, the EU chemicals law.
The commitment is in line with the Commission’s 2025 European Water Resilience Strategy and new EU-wide microplastics and water-efficiency targets. It also fits the EIB Group’s Climate Adaptation Plan and Water Resilience Programme. The fund targets pollution prevention, clean-water processes, circular water systems and climate-resilient resource use. “Targeting innovation in water technology that can help us to recycle, re-use or use more efficiently the water that is available, can be an important signal for both the market and policy makers,” said Falkstedt.

Why It Matters
The €30 million gives PureTerra II capital for the pilot-to-deployment step, which van Schelven calls Europe’s constraint. That lets the fund back companies selling advanced treatment to buyers with fixed regulatory deadlines. It positions PureTerra II to turn wastewater and PFAS compliance spending into portfolio exits, if its technologies scale in time.

articles.title: Singapore Airlines Secures Up to 4,800 Tonnes of Waste Gas SAF from Aether’s Singapore Plant
articles.summary:
Singapore Airlines (SIA) will buy up to 4,800 tonnes of next-generation sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) from Aether Fuels under a binding agreement. Deliveries will run over three years, starting in […]
The post Singapore Airlines Secures Up to 4,800 Tonnes of Waste Gas SAF from Aether’s Singapore Plant appeared first on ESG News.
articles.full_text:
Singapore Airlines Secures Up to 4,800 Tonnes of Waste Gas SAF from Aether’s Singapore Plant
- Offtake volume: Singapore Airlines will buy up to 4,800 tonnes of next-generation SAF from Aether over three years, with deliveries from 2028.
- Waste-gas feedstock: Project Beacon will turn biomethane and industrial waste gases into jet fuel using Aether’s Aurora technology.
- Scale-up plan: Aether intends to start a plant at least 10 times larger than Beacon by 2031.
Singapore Airlines (SIA) will buy up to 4,800 tonnes of next-generation sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) from Aether Fuels under a binding agreement. Deliveries will run over three years, starting in 2028. The fuel will come from Project Beacon, Aether’s commercial production facility, and SIA is the first airline to buy SAF from the plant.
Project Beacon is being developed at Aster’s refining complex on Pulau Bukom in Singapore. It will use feedstocks such as biomethane and industrial waste gases, processed with Aether’s proprietary Aurora technology. That technology innovates around the Fischer-Tropsch process, a method that turns gases into liquid fuel. “Supporting the development and adoption of SAF, and securing future supplies, are integral to SIA’s ambition of achieving net zero carbon emissions by 2050. As the first airline to purchase SAF from Project Beacon, SIA is demonstrating demand for new lower-carbon fuel production pathways in Singapore. We will continue to work with partners globally to scale SAF production, strengthen the aviation industry’s sustainability ecosystem, and support the transition to more sustainable air travel,” said Lee Wen Fen, Chief Sustainability Officer, Singapore Airlines.
Quick anonymous worklife pollWhat's my daily work emissions burn, or savings?Powered by ESG News
Aether presents its route as an alternative to the hydro-processed esters and fatty acids (HEFA) pathway, which relies on more constrained lipid-based feedstocks. The SAF will also be certified under the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA). By 2031, Aether intends to start its first large-scale commercial plant, with capacity at least 10 times larger than Beacon. However, the companies did not disclose the price, total contract value or Project Beacon’s planned production capacity.
What’s New
The binding agreement follows a memorandum of understanding (MOU) that SIA and Aether signed last year. It is also SIA’s first purchase of SAF made with technology that converts waste carbon feedstocks into aviation fuel. “When we signed our MOU with Singapore Airlines last year, Project Beacon had not yet been announced. Since then, we have selected Singapore as the home of our first commercial facility and built critical partnerships across the local value chain. Singapore is building a strong ecosystem for aviation decarbonisation through refining and aviation infrastructure, investment support, sustainability policies, and utilising their position as a global aviation hub. This binding agreement is an important next step and a strong signal of committed demand from a leading global airline – exactly the type of collaboration needed to create the commercial conditions to bring new SAF pathways to scale,” said Conor Madigan, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer, Aether Fuels.
Why It Matters
For SIA, the deal locks in CORSIA-certified fuel from a waste-gas pathway from 2028, supporting its goal of net zero carbon emissions by 2050. For Aether, the contract gives Beacon a committed airline buyer before production begins. That positions Aether to use the SIA deal as a reference when signing offtakers for its planned 2031 plant, provided Beacon delivers on schedule.

articles.title: Two-Thirds of Investors Weigh Responsible AI: Morgan Stanley Survey
articles.summary:
Two-thirds of institutional investors now treat responsible artificial intelligence (AI) as part of their sustainable investing strategy. The finding comes from the Morgan Stanley Institute for Sustainable Investing’s 2026 Sustainable […]
The post Two-Thirds of Investors Weigh Responsible AI: Morgan Stanley Survey appeared first on ESG News.
articles.full_text:
Two-Thirds of Investors Weigh Responsible AI: Morgan Stanley Survey
- Responsible AI uptake: 66% of 900 institutional investors include responsible AI in their sustainable investing strategies.
- Governance focus: 61% of investors prioritizing AI focus on board oversight, ethical AI policies and cybersecurity controls.
- Slower allocation growth: Only 2% of asset owners and 4% of asset managers expect gains above 10 percentage points.
Two-thirds of institutional investors now treat responsible artificial intelligence (AI) as part of their sustainable investing strategy. The finding comes from the Morgan Stanley Institute for Sustainable Investing’s 2026 Sustainable Signals survey. It polled 900 asset owners and asset managers across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific between August and October 2026. Almost all respondents (94%) fold responsible AI into existing themes such as climate adaptation, rather than treating it separately.
Uptake of responsible AI is highest in Europe at 72%, compared with 59% in North America. Among investors prioritizing AI, 61% focus on how companies govern its adoption. Their priorities are board oversight and capabilities, responsible and ethical AI policies, and cybersecurity controls. Fewer concentrate on large language model (LLM) providers, the developers of generative AI systems, or on AI’s wider economic impacts.
More than 80% of respondents expect to raise sustainable allocations over the next two years. However, only 2% of asset owners and 4% of asset managers expect growth above 10 percentage points, compared with about one-fifth in 2025. Morgan Stanley did not disclose the split between asset owners and managers or the margin of error. “Our annual global survey of institutional investors indicates that a majority expect to increase sustainable investment allocations in the coming years, recognizing growth opportunities and the rising materiality of sustainability-related risks,” said Jessica Alsford, Chief Sustainability Officer and Chair of the Institute for Sustainable Investing at Morgan Stanley.
RELATED ARTICLE: 88% of Global Investors Show Interest in Sustainable Investing: Morgan Stanley Survey
What’s New Since 2025
Concerns have eased since 2025, but 64% now call data availability and consistency a very significant concern, up from 47%. More than two-thirds also cite portfolio risk reduction as a reason to invest sustainably, up from half last year. Meanwhile, climate adaptation and resilience has become the top theme, cited by 59% against 52% for climate mitigation.
“In 2026, a consistent picture has emerged across our Sustainable Signals series – with individuals, corporates and institutional investors all showing high levels of continued commitment to sustainability, yet at a more measured pace and with a sharper focus on managing risk,” Alsford said.
Who It Affects
- Data center operators: 24% of the 590 investors incorporating AI review its carbon and water footprint and data centers’ effect on local communities.
- Asset managers: More than 90% of respondents say sustainable investing options are a key factor in awarding or winning mandates.
- Climate data providers: Almost 90% find physical climate impacts on assets hard to evaluate, up from 66%, citing scarce high-quality localized data.

articles.summary:

articles.full_text:
Google Hackathon Winners Target Solar Siting, Wildfire Shutoffs and Grid Hardening in Colorado
- Second annual event: Google held the second annual Colorado Impact Hackathon at its Boulder offices with CU Boulder and the Colorado Energy Office.
- Top prize: SolarSnap, an AI app built to help homeowners plan solar panel setups, took first place.
- Grid resilience entries: Grid Watch and Grid Guard placed second and third with tools for wildfire shutoffs and grid hardening.
Google hosted the second annual Colorado Impact Hackathon at its Boulder offices, where students worked on one question. They were asked how Colorado can create a clean, secure and resilient electric grid. The company ran the event in partnership with CU Boulder and the Colorado Energy Office.
First place went to SolarSnap, an artificial intelligence (AI) app for homeowners. It uses a phone’s camera to help users find the ideal setup for solar panels. Grid Watch placed second with an AI-managed battery network. The system is designed to keep power on during wildfire shutoffs while also reducing electricity costs.
Grid Guard took third place with predictive capabilities for targeted grid hardening, meaning upgrades that make the grid more resistant to damage. Google also cited wildfire risk and energy backlogs as state problems the event set out to address.
Colorado Attorney General Phil Weiser spoke at the event. Andrew Mayock, Vice Chancellor for Sustainability at CU Boulder, also addressed participants. Both highlighted the importance of bold innovation in shaping Colorado’s clean energy future. Google did not disclose how many students took part, the judging criteria or whether winners will get support to develop their projects.

Who It Affects
- Homeowners weighing solar: SolarSnap is pitched as a phone-based way to find the right panel setup for a home before installation.
- Households in wildfire shutoff zones: Grid Watch targets power loss during wildfire shutoffs and also aims to lower electricity costs.
- Grid planners and the Colorado Energy Office: Grid Guard uses prediction to target hardening at specific parts of the grid.

articles.summary:

The post Electric Barge for Nike Cargo in Vietnam Targets 778 Tons of Annual CO2 Savings appeared first on ESG News.
articles.full_text:
Electric Barge for Nike Cargo in Vietnam Targets 778 Tons of Annual CO2 Savings
- Inland route: The barge runs a 180-kilometer round trip between Nike’s Ho Chi Minh City drop-off and Gemalink.
- CO2 savings: The barge is expected to avoid about 778 tons of CO2 a year.
- Solar charging: A solar farm at Gemalink powers charging, with CATL batteries recharging in about four hours.
CMA CGM, Nike and Gemadept have launched a fully electric barge in Vietnam to carry Nike cargo by inland waterway. It links Nike’s inland drop-off location in Ho Chi Minh City with Gemalink, Gemadept’s deep-sea terminal in Cai Mep. The companies expect the barge to avoid about 778 tons of carbon dioxide emissions a year. It runs on batteries recharged with certified renewable electricity.
The route covers a 180-kilometer round trip from a drop-off site formerly in Binh Duong province. The barge is designed to carry more than 50,000 TEUs (twenty-foot equivalent units, a standard container measure) a year. As a result, it gives Nike a lower-carbon alternative to road transport for inland cargo, supporting its supply chain decarbonization efforts. “Reducing emissions across a global supply chain takes more than any one company. It takes new ideas, strong partnerships and a willingness to rethink how we operate,” said Cimarron Nix, Chief Sustainability Officer at NIKE, Inc. “This project with CMA CGM and Gemadept is a great example of how we can work together to turn innovation into practical solutions that reduce our impact while building a more resilient supply chain.”
Quick anonymous worklife pollWhat's my daily work emissions burn, or savings?Powered by ESG News
CMA CGM’s New Build and R&D teams developed the barge, which uses battery technology from CATL. It recharges in about four hours at dedicated charging infrastructure at Gemalink, supplied by a solar farm at the terminal. The partners did not disclose the project’s investment cost or the solar farm’s generating capacity. “As a leading port and logistics operator in Vietnam, Gemadept believes that the future of sustainable logistics depends on stronger connections among ports, inland waterways and clean energy. The launch of this fully electric barge with CMA CGM and Nike marks an important milestone in bringing that vision to life. By integrating electric transport, dedicated charging infrastructure and renewable energy at Gemalink, the project demonstrates how partnership and innovation can turn sustainability ambitions into practical solutions. We believe this model has strong potential to be expanded and replicated, contributing to the long-term transition towards low-carbon logistics in Vietnam,” said Do Cong Khanh, Deputy Chief Executive Officer of Gemadept Corporation and Chairman of Gemalink Deep-Sea Port.
CMA CGM in Vietnam
CMA CGM has operated in Vietnam since 2006, with five offices and more than 220 employees. It also runs 29 weekly mainline services calling at seven Vietnamese ports, backed by an intermodal network with CEVA Logistics. “Decarbonizing global supply chains requires moving beyond ambition to deliver concrete, scalable solutions. This fully electric barge is a powerful example of what can be achieved when shipping companies, customers and terminal operators combine their expertise and commitment. Together with Nike and Gemadept, we are demonstrating that innovative, lower-carbon inland transportation solutions are already within reach. Now, CMA CGM aims to build on this success to accelerate their deployment across other markets and supply chains,” said Christine Cabau, Executive Vice President Assets and Operations at CMA CGM.

Why It Matters
For CMA CGM, the barge is an in-house model designed to be replicated in other geographies and customer supply chains. Nike gets a renewable-powered link for inland cargo, while Gemadept adds a solar-backed charging hub at Gemalink. If the charging setup can be repeated at other terminals, the model could become an electric inland service CMA CGM offers other shippers.
